resources.string: Test build. Only for checking how reels can be recognised.

Test build. Looks only inside YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook (and their Lite apps) to see which screen is open: the names and positions of screen parts, never words. Nothing leaves your phone unless you share the file yourself.
On, but Android has not started it yet. Reopen this screen, or turn it off and on again.

Android 13 and newer block Accessibility for apps installed from a file. Try to turn on Reelity once, then open App info, tap the three dots (⋮) at the top and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then turn it on again.

If Advanced Protection is on (Settings > Security and privacy > Advanced Protection), Android 17 does not let apps like this test build use Accessibility, and it blocks installing apps from files. Turn it off while you test, and back on afterwards if you want.

This cannot be undone. Export first if you have not sent them yet.
Let Reelity notice when a reel is open
To count reels, and later to stop them when you ask it to, Reelity uses an Android feature called Accessibility.
Only inside YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook (and their Lite apps), and only which screen is open, for example “the reels player”.
Words on the screen, messages, comments, captions, passwords, anything you type, who you follow or which videos you watch. It does not record your screen.
This test build only notices which screen is open, so that reels can be recognised. Counting and the stop screen come in later builds.

When you tap “Reel” or “Not a reel”, it saves the layout of that screen: the internal names of its parts and where they are, plus your phone model and the app version. Never words or pictures. The file stays on this phone until you share it yourself.
Nowhere by itself. Reelity has no internet permission, so it cannot send anything.
Android will then ask whether Reelity can have “full control” of your device. Android shows this to every app that uses Accessibility. Reelity is limited to the apps above.
You can turn this off any time in Settings > Accessibility.
